title: Marketplace Publishing Scenarios and Market Readiness Cheatsheet
body:
Purpose:
Quick, practical playbook for publishing Redwood Inference offers across cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP) that teams can follow during launch sprints. This is intentionally lightweight — copy options + acceptance checkpoints + simple QA scenarios so launch owners can move fast and avoid the common rejections we’ve seen.

How to use this doc:
- Pick the publishing scenario that matches your SKU (hosted api, dedicated, private).
- Run the acceptance checklist for the target marketplace.
- Paste the chosen copy variants into the platform listing template and bake in the tech/legal notes.
- Use the QA scenarios to validate end-to-end listing behavior before submit.

High-level scenarios (pick one):
1) Self-serve hosted API listing (low friction) — SKU: hosted-api-basic / hosted-api-pro
   - Focus: clear pricing per 1K tokens, free trial CTA, link to quickstart, security bullet explaining data handling (no customer data retained).
   - Acceptance bar: docs link live, public API key flow documented, simple usage examples for JS/Python present.

2) Dedicated capacity offer (requires sales-assisted flow) — SKU: dedicated-monthly-commit
   - Focus: benefits (predictable throughput, SLA), commitment terms, contact flow for sales.
   - Acceptance bar: lead capture form verified, legal terms referenced, sample SLA table included.

3) Private deployment / VPC (enterprise-focused) — SKU: private-vpc-enterprise
   - Focus: network diagrams, KMS/HSM integrations, on-prem options and compliance attachments.
   - Acceptance bar: security attachments attached (SOC2 summary, ISO certs), contact for security review, private deployment artifacts available.

Core listing copy sections (short snippets — pick/adapt):
- Short tagline (8–12 words):
  • "High-performance LLM inference with predictable latency and cost."
  • "Run modern LLMs at scale — performance tuned for production."
- One-liner (20–30 words):
  • "Redwood Inference delivers a unified runtime for hosted, dedicated, or private deployments — predictable latency, cost controls, and enterprise-grade observability for LLM applications."
- Top bullets (value props):
  • "Latency SLOs and SLA-backed reserved capacity"
  • "Intelligent batching, caching, and quantization for lower per-token cost"
  • "Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments"
  • "Audit logs, KMS integrations, and role-based access for compliance"
- CTA variants (choose 1):
  • "Start free — quickstart in 5 minutes"
  • "Request a demo & pricing"
  • "Contact sales for dedicated/private options"

Marketplace-specific quicknotes (ops + copy)
- AWS Marketplace:
  • Pricing model: can support metered usage or fixed subscription. For hosted-api we prefer metered (per-token) mapping to AWS metering.
  • Requirements: short descriptive summary (<1000 chars), usage instructions, support contact. Avoid referencing third-party benchmarks.
  • Common rejection reason: ambiguous data-retention language — include explicit: "We do not retain customer inputs or derived outputs except for 30-day troubleshooting logs, removable on request."

- Azure Marketplace:
  • Pricing model: SaaS offer or private plan. For Dedicated we recommend SaaS + lead generation flow.
  • Requirements: legal T&Cs doc, logo guidelines (vector preferred), and required privacy statement link.
  • Common rejection reason: missing enterprise contact and pre-sale flow. Ensure "Contact sales" form is fully functional.

- GCP Marketplace:
  • Pricing models: subscription or usage-based billing (billing pipe required). For private deployments we usually map to "Bring your own license" SKU.
  • Requirements: full product description, support window, technical lead details.
  • Common rejection reason: insufficient deployment docs for VM/ container images; include step-by-step deploy guide.

Acceptance checklist (pre-submit) — run for target marketplace
- [ ] Listing title under 70 chars and compliant with vendor policy
- [ ] Short description and long description proofread (no marketing hyperbole that triggers vendor policy)
- [ ] Pricing mapped to vendor billing model (include sample invoice calculation)
- [ ] Technical quickstart present (code snippet + curl or CLI)
- [ ] Support & escalation path (name/email/SLAs) present
- [ ] Security/compliance attachments uploaded (SOC2 summary, DPA link, ISO where applicable)
- [ ] Logo + screenshots (PNG & SVG) match vendor dimensions and are hosted on stable CDN
- [ ] Legal boilerplate verification (export controls, restricted countries callouts)
- [ ] Contact form / lead flow validated (test leads created and routed)
- [ ] Internal PR created and link added to submission notes

QA scenarios (run on staging listing or with vendor sandbox when available)
- Scenario A — New trial sign-up (hosted-api): user signs up, redeems credit, hits quickstart generating a token; verify tokens provisioned, sample request succeeds, and billing meter increments (or trial flag set).
- Scenario B — Sales workflow (dedicated): submit lead, verify lead enrichment pipeline (SFDC/HubSpot), check assigned SDR gets notification, confirm follow-up email template used.
- Scenario C — Private deployment request: customer requests on-prem installer; verify that the security review contact is alerted and attachments are delivered via secure link; track as security review ticket.

Launch milestones & owners (example timeline for 2-week sprint)
- Day 0–2: Copy + pricing draft (Owner: Ava)
- Day 3: Assets (logos/screenshots) and compliance attach (Owner: Priya)
- Day 4–6: Vendor staging submission + internal QA (Owner: Noah)
- Day 7–10: Vendor feedback loop & fixes (Owner: Jordan)
- Day 11–14: Final submit & monitor (Owner: Marisol)

Risk mitigation notes (common fail points + remediations)
- Risk: Data retention phrasing triggers vendor legal.
  • Mitigation: Use conservative explicit phrasing and link to DPA; have legal pre-approve.
- Risk: Pricing model doesn't map cleanly to vendor metering.
  • Mitigation: Add worked examples and internal SKU mapping table.
- Risk: Contact flow not routed to the right team.
  • Mitigation: End-to-end test with staged lead and runbook for owner.

Copy experiments to A/B on listing pages (ideas)
- Experiment 1: Emphasize cost ("Lower per-token cost with intelligent batching") vs emphasize reliability ("SLA-backed latency for user-facing apps"). Measure CTR on "Start free".
- Experiment 2: CTA wording — "Start free" vs "Request demo" for dedicated SKUs. Measure lead quality.

Notes to legal and security reviewers (tactical):
- Include the SOC2 summary PDF and a short one-page security FAQ that addresses network isolation, encryption at rest/in-transit, and key management.
- Flag export-control restrictions early if customers in restricted countries request private deployment.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical SKU names for "hosted-api-pro" vs "hosted-api-enterprise" (affects billing mapping).
- Confirm which sample invoices we want to show for AWS metered billing. (Action: Noah)
- Finalize the DPA link to be used in every listing (Action: Priya)

Appendix: sample short listing copy (paste-ready)
Title: Redwood Inference — High-performance LLM inference
Short: Run modern LLMs with predictable latency, cost controls, and enterprise observability.
Long: Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for serving LLMs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Our runtime optimizes latency and throughput with batching, caching, and quantization suggestions so your apps stay fast and economical. Get started with our free trial or contact sales for dedicated/private deployments and SLAs.
